title: REQ-20261111-OPS004 — Hardship payment calculation: $10,000 gross, 6% tax-free, $2,068 PAYG withheld, $7,932 net (Tom Bradley)
content:
Payment calculation for the severe financial hardship release on Caldova Super (Essential) CS-1030412 — Tom Bradley, age 47.

Amount: Tom requested $15,000. The maximum single severe financial hardship release is $10,000 gross (minimum $1,000), once in any 12-month period, so the recommended outcome is a PARTIAL approval of $10,000 gross. The remaining $5,000 cannot be released under this condition of release. Team Leader approval is required before release (vulnerable member).

Account tax components before payment: balance $84,300 — tax-free component $5,058 (6%); taxable component (taxed element) $79,242 (94%). Under the proportioning rule every payment carries the same 6% / 94% split.

Calculation:
• Gross payment: $10,000
• Tax-free component (6%): $600
• Taxable component, taxed element (94%): $9,400
• PAYG withheld — Tom is under 60 (and under preservation age), so 22% (20% + 2% Medicare levy) applies to the taxed element: $9,400 × 22% = $2,068
• Net payment: $10,000 − $2,068 = $7,932

Payment: $7,932 to Tom's nominated account (name 'Thomas Bradley', account ending 7741 — payee name and BSB match ✅), scheduled for Fri 13 Nov 2026 after approval. The $2,068 withheld is remitted to the ATO and shown on a PAYG payment summary. Withholding is not necessarily the final tax: the taxable component is included in Tom's tax return and taxed at the lower of his marginal rate and 20% plus Medicare levy, so some of the tax may be refunded when he lodges.

Redemption plan (Investment Solutions): use Caldova Cash Account money above the 1% minimum first, then sell Balanced model units for the rest (0.10% sell spread applies). Expected balance after payment: about $74,300, before market movements and transaction costs.

Next eligibility: no further severe financial hardship release can be paid before 13 Nov 2027 (12 months after this payment), and only if the criteria are met again. Release on compassionate grounds — for example to prevent foreclosure on his home — is a separate application decided by the ATO.
